newsitem.title: USA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, Nov 25 - Puerto Cortes - Vessels berthed, 2 discharging/loading containers, 2 discharging fertiliser, 1 discharging wheat, 1 loading bananas. Vessels waiting, 3 to discharge/load containers, 1 to load bananas, 1 to discharge sbm. Corn and wheat vessels due, 3 to discharge/load containers, 4 to discharge/load generals, 1 to discharge petroleum products, 1 to discharge wood, 3 to load bananas. Four vessels berthed of which 1 discharging/loading containers, 2 discharging fertiliser, 1 discharging wheat. 15 Due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas, 1 to discharge fertiliser, 1 to discharge soy/wheat. No delays expected.

MEXICO, Nov 26 - Tampico - Vessels in port 2 general cargo, 2 sugar, 1 cement, 2 corn, 1 repairs, 3 vessels anchored of which 2 general cargo, 1 container, working normally. Altamira - Vessels in port 1 heavy pieces, 1 container vessel, 1 repairs, working normally. Veracruz - Vessels in port, 3 corn, 4 grain, 1 sugar, 1 repair, 1 container vessel, 2 pipes, 1 fertiliser, working normally. Manzanillo - Vessels in port, 2 general cargo, 1 cars, 2 containers, 1 fertiliser, 1 oil tanker, working normally. Coatzacoalcos - Vessels in port, oil tankers, 5 chemicals, 1 repairs, working normally.

PANAMA, Nov 25 - Balboa - Two tankers operating. Cristobal - Vessels operating 1 bulker, 3 containers, 1 tanker. Panama Canal waterway at full capacity and transit booking system allocation normal. 36 vessels due, 22 in queue, 6 booked, 37 scheduled.

UNITED STATES, Nov 25 - Hampton Roads, VA - Four general cargo/container vessels in pier operating, 4 bulkers in pier loading coal, 3 anchored waiting to load. 1 Bulker discharging cement, 1 bulker loading scrap, 1 bulker loading fertiliser, 2 vessels in pier under repair and/or layberth. 1 Vessel anchored under repair. Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating, 6 bulkers, 3 container vessels, 1 ro/ro, 1 auto vessel, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo. No cable vessels on standby, 3 vessels in repair yards, 3 bulkers awaiting berth of which 1 to load coke breeze, 1 to discharge sugar, 1 other. Jersey City, NJ - One vessel in port. Port Newark, NJ - Two vessels. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Three vessels.

East coast Baltimore, MD - Nov 26 - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week, no adverse conditions, at CD canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well, no delays. Average waiting time Consol Coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No vessels due at shipyard river coal terminal or grain elevator during the next week, no delays expected at tanker terminals. All terminals up and running. Vessels due on 28/11. Columbus street, North Charleston and Wando Terminal will be light. No navigation problems in the harbour. New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, container or tanker terminals no congestion at sugar terminals.

Norfolk, VA - Ten vessels due at Norfolk Southern coal pier this week. 3 Vessels anchored waiting to load, 11 due at Dominion terminal, 4 vessels due at pier IX coal terminal, no vessels due at Cargill. Container and general cargo terminals working normally, no delays oil and bulk terminals, working normally, all channels are opening with prevailing depths available. Philadelphia, PA - No port congestion, or at Camden, Wilmington, no activity regarding dredging/repairs/navigational problems. Savannah, GA - No congestion expected at Garden City terminals (container port), Ocean terminals (breakbulk) for coming week. 1-2 Days delay for vessels at Colonial Marine terminals. All liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no congestion expected, navigational conditions remain normal.

Gulf Coast - Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Houston and Galveston grain elevators congestion at some oil/chemical terminals night and morning fog causes the ship channel to close and reopens late a.m. New Orleans, LA - Rain causes delays for grain loading. River stage is at 8.4 feet, expected to rise to 9 ft. Normal transit times can be expected. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi River gulf outlet will be 34 ft. Present max permissible draft at sw pass is 47 ft. Fw. For vessels under 100,000 dwt 46 ft. Fw. For vessels over 100,000 dwt. Some elevators are not working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments.

West coast Columbia River/Portland - Heavy rain and snow has affected the grain loading productions at all Columbia River elevators this week. There are currently 14 grain vessels in the Columbia River district of which 7 loading, 7 waiting average waiting time is approx. 3-5 Days. Coos bay - Vessel traffic extremely slow this past week. 1 Woodchip was delayed due to flooding in the channel, 1 lumber vessel working at export services.

Los Angeles, CA - Metropolitan looks moderately busy for December 2-3 days delay expected at anchor awaiting berth. Koch carbon 1 vessel due in December. Kaiser moderately busy for December. Two to three days delay for coal/petcoke awaiting berth. Bulk cargoes will be moderately busy. San Francisco, CA - delays are to be expected due to fog. Rain may affect transit up the river, depending on how the state will control the reservoir run-off. Japan rice is starting to move from both Sacramento and Stockton. Honolulu, HI - Traffic is medium in both Barbers Point and Honolulu harbour.
